A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGDS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and relocation in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments on Gaussian mixtures, Manywell distributions, Lennard-Jones potentials, and alanine dipeptide, including ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds tripeptide and tetrapeptide evaluations, RND-weight sensitivity results, and a parallel-tempering experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the TB objectives, RND mechanism, replay, and re-initialization remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds a Searcher variant using parallel-tempering molecular dynamics with replica exchanges; v1 mentioned parallel tempering only as a possible future enhancement.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 extends all-atom molecular conformer evaluation from alanine dipeptide alone to larger alanine tripeptide and tetrapeptide systems, reported as 33 and 43 atoms. This substantially broadens molecular-size coverage while retaining the Gaussian-mixture, Manywell, and Lennard-Jones tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes TB, TB+LS, TB+LS+LP, and TB+Expl+LP from the Manywell-64/128 comparisons, although these remain in the lower-dimensional Table 6. Table 2 adds Adjoint Sampling using results attributed to its published paper. Appendix B.4 also introduces a parallel-tempering-plus-MLE control.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds position and energy-histogram Wasserstein-2 evaluation. New protocols include testing RND weights at 20% of second-round training and matching energy budgets in the parallel-tempering comparison. Section 5.3 also changes the reported dipeptide atom count from 22 to 23 without explaining whether this corrects the description or reflects different inputs.

E4.justification: Existing component ablations and the Manywell debiasing analysis are retained. New Appendix B.3 tests RND weights from 1 to 1,000 on Manywell-128, LJ-13, LJ-55, and dipeptide. Appendix B.4 tests whether the advantage over MLE persists with a parallel-tempering Searcher, substantially extending sensitivity and component-replacement evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions already state that experiments use four random seeds and report uncertainty values. The new checklist explicitly identifies table uncertainties as standard deviations. No increased run count or formal significance test is documented, and the new RND-sensitivity Table 7 provides only point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds peptide results, LJ Wasserstein scores, sensitivity results, and parallel-tempering results. For example, Table 3 reports SGDS gaps of 5.60 ± 0.03 and 26.60 ± 0.21, in units of 1,000, for tripeptide and tetrapeptide. Retained Table 1 and Table 6 scores are unchanged, while several Manywell comparator rows and separate LJ/dipeptide ELBO and EUBO entries are removed.

T1.justification: The SDE and trajectory-balance formulation, AIS/MALA derivations, ELBO/EUBO reasoning, and target-energy definitions are retained. The added empirical metrics and parallel-tempering description introduce no new formal definitions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the claimed molecular demonstration from alanine dipeptide to di-, tri-, and tetrapeptides. The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about scalable, sample-efficient training, exploration through RND, and mitigation of primacy bias.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly argues that RND weights require little calibration, and B.4 interprets the added experiment as demonstrating compatibility with advanced Searchers. Appendix C remains unchanged, including its warning that RND requires careful tuning; this warning is not fully reconciled with the new robustness language.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous repository to the named SGDS GitHub repository. The appendix adds explanations of baseline abbreviations, extends molecular configurations to the added peptides, and describes the partial-training calibration rule. Most architecture, budget, and iDEM implementation details were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Havens et al.'s Adjoint Sampling and Sugita and Okamoto's replica-exchange molecular dynamics, incorporating them into comparisons and Searcher discussion. The broader positioning relative to GFlowNets, Lemos et al., and Sendera et al. is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include localized baseline and molecular-results rewrites, a notation subsection, two supplementary-analysis subsections, a NeurIPS checklist, and updated equal-contribution and conference information. These additions do not substantially reorganize the research narrative.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially revised: Table 1 loses rows, Table 2 replaces separate bounds with Wasserstein columns, and Table 3 is organized across three peptides. Figure 4 replaces repeated dipeptide examples with three peptide-specific rows and moves earlier. Tables 7 and 8 are new, while existing appendix figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The larger-peptide evaluations, distributional metrics, and targeted sensitivity and Searcher tests strengthen empirical support for SGDS. The net gain is limited by removing several Manywell comparisons, including the closest Manywell-64 gap baseline, and separate bound values. The RND robustness interpretation also exceeds what its early-training point estimates establish and remains in tension with the unchanged tuning limitation.
